# Example: choosing headphones

Hypothetical request: “Find me wireless headphones under ₹10,000 for work and travel.” No product recommendations or prices are implied.

The budget and intended use are explicit. A trade-off likely to change the shortlist is whether the user prioritizes microphone quality for calls or noise cancellation on flights. “Lightweight” may also matter, but should not be assumed to be essential. Ask a focused question: “For this purchase, which matters more: clear calls in a noisy room or reducing airplane noise? If both are essential, say so.”

An editable brief might show: maximum ₹10,000, work and travel, selected priority, unknown comfort and return requirements, compare options with evidence, no purchase authorized. If available choices force a compromise, show it instead of silently relaxing the budget or treating an inference as a requirement. If the user wants a quick exploratory shortlist, proceed with clearly labeled assumptions and no purchase.
